card.name: Garia
card.tagline: Tripuri sowing-season dance praying for a good harvest
card.profile: Garia (or Goria) is a folk dance of the Tripuri and Jamatia tribes of Tripura, performed during the Garia Puja festival in April that marks the commencement of the jhum (shifting cultivation) sowing season (Wikipedia, Dances of Tripura; Tripura State Portal). The festival begins with the worship of Lord Garia (Baba Garia), the deity of livestock and wealth, by the Ochai (tribal priest), followed by dancing by both men and women from village to village in a gradually increasing tempo, with mudras that mimic agricultural and natural movements (Wikipedia; Adivasi Lives Matter). It is accompanied by drums, the bamboo flute, sarinda and bamboo cymbals; celebrations continue for about seven days (Wikipedia).
card.insight: A bamboo pole symbolising Lord Garia is worshipped with flowers and garlands; offerings include cotton thread, rice, fowl, eggs and rice beer, and during the festival no one may cross the shadow of the symbolic deity for fear of angering him (Indian Holiday; Tripura Tourism).
card.image_significance: The sowing-season prayer dance. A representative image shows ornate costume and expressive hand-gesture (mudra) detail — Tripura (Tripuri), India.
